conventions.convention: Assume AC, finite K ≥ 1, prescheduled information fractions 0 < t₁ < ⋯ < tK = 1, and α ∈ (0,1). Spending functions need only be nondecreasing, with A(0) = 0 and A(1) = α.
The stipulated simple-null vector is centered Gaussian with covariance Σjk = √(tj/tk) for j ≤ k, extended symmetrically. Exact calibration concerns this joint law and planned looks.
One-sided rejection uses Zj ≥ bj; symmetric two-sided rejection uses |Zj| ≥ cj and is calibrated separately. The procedure stops at its first crossing.
A zero spending increment receives boundary +∞ and an empty crossing event; a positive increment is calibrated by the cumulative union equation.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC and the canonical group-sequential design. The recursive boundary algorithm is well-defined: every positive spending increment has a unique finite boundary, while a zero increment has boundary +∞. For every k, the probability under P₀ of a rejection by look k is A(tk). This holds for one-sided upper boundaries and separately calibrated symmetric two-sided crossings, under the specified Gaussian null law and prescheduled fractions.

A finite prescheduled canonical Gaussian design uses a nondecreasing A:[0,1]→[0,α] with A(0)=0 and A(1)=α, covariance Σjk=√(tj/tk) for j≤k, and first-crossing rejection with either one-sided upper boundaries or symmetric two-sided boundaries.

Process k=1,…,K in order. At a flat spending increment assign +∞ and leave the cumulative rejection event unchanged. At a positive increment choose the boundary solving P₀(Rk−1 ∪ {Zk ≥ bk})=A(tk), or P₀(Rk−1 ∪ {|Zk| ≥ ck})=A(tk) with ck≥0 in symmetric two-sided mode.
